newsitem.title: UK: Matra BAe Dynamics signs 700 mln stg defence deal.
newsitem.headline: Matra BAe Dynamics signs 700 mln stg defence deal.

text.p: Matra BAe Dynamics said on Tuesday it had signed a contract worth over 700 million pounds ($1.14 billion) with Britain's Ministry of Defence to develop and produce the Storm Shadow anti-attack missile, sealing a deal originally announced last summer.
Matra BAe Dynamics is a 50-50 joint venture between British Aerospace Plc and the Matra arm of France's Lagardere SCA.
The firm said in a statement that further production option quantities could substantially increase the contract's value.
The Storm Shadow is an advanced air-launched cruise stealth missile based on Matra's Apache weapon.

It will produce long range firepower for the Royal Air Force's Tornado EF2000 and Harrier GR7 aircraft, ensuring air crew no longer have to enter heavily defended enemy airspace in order to destroy high value targets.
The firm said British industry would gain substantial quality work on the programme at its sites in Stevenage, Bristol and Lostock and also at over 80 subcontractors across Britain.
Other firms involved with work on the contract include British Aerospace Royal Ordnance, GEC Marconi Sensors and Microturbo (UK) Ltd.
"This is an excellent step forward for our new company and will provide high technology work for our people for many years to come," said Matra BAe Dynamics chief executive Noel Forgeard.

"The award proves Europe has the capability to develop and produce the next generation of weapon system for our armed forces. We also believe there are good export prospects for the weapon," he added.

Matra BAe Dynamics, which is Europe's largest guided weapons business with annual turnover of some 1.0 billion pounds and a workforce of some 6,000 in Britain and France, was formally set up last November.
